subject: Request: Reclassify committed throughput + evidence for change order
messages:
From: SanoTech <contracts@sanotech.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Miriam Cole <miriam.cole@lawfirm.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Change request: reclassify committed throughput to 'burstable' pool + pricing impact

Hi Aditya,

Following our internal capacity planning, SanoTech needs to reclassify 400K token/month from the fixed committed tier in Exhibit B into a burstable pool for Q4. The ask: convert 400K (current monthly committed) to a shared burst band for 3 months, with a request to pro-rate fees and apply the previously-discussed one-time implementation credit.

We need three things to push this through with procurement and legal here:
- A short change order (1 page) describing the reclassification and the reduced monthly minimum for Oct–Dec.
- Evidence/redline showing impact to invoice schedule.
- SOC2/retention confirmation that data flows and logs for burst traffic will remain in the same assurances (we need an evidence stub for our audit).

I attached a one-page request summary. Can you confirm whether this is eligible under our MSA change control (Section 3.2) and provide a draft change order we can circulate on our side?

Thanks,
--
Collin Reyes
Head of Procurement, SanoTech
contracts@sanotech.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Collin Reyes <contracts@sanotech.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, miriam.cole@lawfirm.com
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Change request: reclassify committed throughput to 'burstable' pool + pricing impact

Hi Collin — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. We're happy to help. Quick answers up front:
- This is a change-of-scope/orderform amendment (Section 3.2 of the MSA) and is eligible for a change order.
- We can draft a 1-page change order that: (a) reclassifies 400K tokens/month to the burstable band for Oct–Dec 2027, (b) shows pro-rated fees and an implementation credit line, and (c) confirms that all existing security controls and log retention remain unchanged.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I'll put together a draft change order and send to your legal (Miriam) and our legal ops.
2) Laura (pricing/ops) — can you confirm pro-rated fee calc and the one-time credit amount (we previously discussed $12k implementation credit) and attach the invoice impact table?
3) Connor (contracts) — mind owning the MSA cross-check and signature path? We may need a shortened DocuSign route given this is timeboxed (3 months).

Collin — if you can confirm acceptance in principle by EOD Wednesday (13 Oct) we'll aim to push a signed change order by next week.

Thanks,

--
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Collin Reyes <contracts@sanotech.com>, Miriam Cole <miriam.cole@lawfirm.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Oct 2027 08:26:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Change request: reclassify committed throughput to 'burstable' pool + pricing impact

Aditya / Connor — quick catch-up. I ran the pro‑rata and credit math and attached an invoice-impact table. Summary:
- Baseline committed fee for 400K tokens/month = $48,000/month (at current tiered rates).
- Pro-rate Oct (prorated to 20 days) = $32,000; Nov/Dec full months moved to burst usage (we estimate billing to shift to pay-as-you-go for any overage beyond their remaining committed balance).
- Implementation credit (one-time) = $12,000 applied in the first post-change invoice.

I also asked infra for a short security statement confirming that burst traffic is served by the same dedicated runtime with identical logging and KV-cache retention policies. Jonas Weber in Applied ML will provide a 1-paragraph confirmation for audit; Connor, can you confirm the MSA cross-reference language for the change order so Miriam can review redlines?

Attachment stubs: sano_invoice_impact_20271012.xlsx, infra-security-burst-stub.txt

Laura
--
Laura Bennett
Pricing Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Collin Reyes <contracts@sanotech.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Miriam Cole <miriam.cole@lawfirm.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Change request: reclassify committed throughput to 'burstable' pool + pricing impact

Collin — thanks for the patience. Per our internal review:
- MSA Section 3.2 allows Order Form amendments via a written Change Order signed by both parties. I recommend the following short language for the change order (we'll include in the draft):
  "This Change Order modifies Exhibit B of the Order Form dated 2027-01-11 between Redwood Inference and SanoTech to reclassify 400,000 tokens/month from the Committed Throughput band to the Burstable Throughput band for the period 2027-10-01 through 2027-12-31. All other terms of the Agreement remain unchanged. Invoices will reflect pro-rated committed fees and a one-time implementation credit of $12,000 applied to the invoice following execution."

- Attached: a draft change order (proposed-change-order-draft.docx) and the invoice impact spreadsheet.
- Jonas (cc) — can you confirm the infra-security paragraph off your stub so we can include it verbatim for SanoTech audit?

Collin — Miriam: if your team is OK with the draft language we can route to DocuSign; suggested signer path: Collin (SanoTech Contracts) -> Miriam (SanoTech Legal ack) -> Connor (Redwood VP Finance) -> Aditya (Redwood Sales) for countersign. We can shorten to two internal signers if SanoTech prefers faster routing.

If I don't hear objections by end of day Friday we'll upload to DocuSign and send for signature.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com
